context:
Follow existing test patterns in tests/unit/{cli,core,tpcdi,platforms} and
prefer fast unit tests with mocks over integration tests. Implement coverage
lift in waves ordered by fastest impact (near-50% quick wins first, then
medium-effort modules, then large modules requiring 5-10 tests each, then
CLI, then TPC-DI). Recompute and checkpoint coverage after each wave using
coverage.json plus the per-file checker to keep progress measurable.

Naming convention: new files are named test_{module}_coverage.py when an
existing test file covers the same source module. All tests marked
@pytest.mark.fast and @pytest.mark.unit, pure mocks only.

Within each phase, batches are independent and can be parallelized via
Task agents. Each batch creates all its test files, then runs verification
before proceeding to the next phase.
description:
Close remaining test coverage gaps by enforcing a per-module >=50% floor for
active benchbox/ modules while temporarily deferring a small set of
legacy/demo/heavy-parser files.

The HTML coverage report (2026-02-08, 59.59% overall) identifies ~67 modules
below 50%. This plan provides a concrete per-file implementation sequence
with specific test file names, estimated test counts, and batch groupings
for parallel execution.

Implementation sequence (8 phases):
  1. Add active-scope per-file coverage checker and Makefile workflow.
  2. Quick wins - modules at 43-49% needing 2-4 tests each (~21 files).
  3. Medium effort - tuning, credentials, TPC runners, platform adapters (~20 files).
  4. High effort - large modules requiring 5-10 tests each (~11 files).
  5. CLI coverage - zero-coverage through near-50% CLI modules (~20 files).
  6. Active TPC-DI modules under 50% (not deferred).
  7. Final sweep - fill any remaining gaps found after verification.
  8. Enforce the gate in local CI workflow and keep deferred-module tracking.

Total: ~87 new test files, ~405 test functions.

anti_patterns.dont: add integration tests that require cloud credentials or external services
import heavy cloud SDKs at module level in test files
anti_patterns.why: they add 2-5s import overhead and may not be installed

anti_patterns.instead: assert observable behavior and error-path contracts

anti_patterns.dont: silently defer additional modules beyond the approved list
anti_patterns.instead: add any new deferment as explicit TODO update
test query structure, table references, and parameters instead
anti_patterns.why: SQL formatting changes would cause false failures
